 Learn more Medical Properties Trust reported third quarter 2026 revenue of US$250.14 million and net income of US$201.58 million, compared with a net loss in the same period a year earlier, with basic earnings per share from continuing operations of US$0.34. 
 The real estate investment trust also recorded net income of US$231.82 million for the first nine months of 2026, a shift from a loss in the prior-year period. This highlights how recent portfolio and tenant changes are feeding into reported profitability. 
 We will now look at how Medical Properties Trust's return to profitability in the quarter could reshape its existing investment narrative.

 Medical Properties Trust Investment Narrative Recap 
 To hold Medical Properties Trust, you need to believe the hospital portfolio can keep generating reliable rent while management works through tenant transitions and debt. The third quarter return to profit, with US$201.58 million of net income and US$0.34 in basic EPS from continuing operations, supports that rental model in the near term but does not remove execution risk. 
 The key short term catalyst is consistent cash rent from restructured and re-tenanted hospitals, especially where operators previously showed stress. The biggest risk remains uneven collections or further concessions, including at behavioral health tenants, which could pressure earnings and make already tight interest coverage more uncomfortable despite the stronger recent results. 
 The fresh data point that matters most here is the scale and quality of earnings in the third quarter of 2026. Medical Properties Trust reported US$250.14 million of revenue, US$231 million of sales and a shift from a loss to US$201.58 million of profit compared with the same period last year, with both basic and diluted EPS from continuing operations at US$0.34. 
 Across the first nine months of 2026, net income of US$231.82 million, compared with a loss a year earlier, gives management more room to keep refinancing and repositioning troubled assets. For you, the question is how durable that profitability is if re-tenanting runs into delays, political risks intensify or variable rent structures deliver weaker cash flow than the headline results suggest. 
 Medical Properties Trust's narrative projects US$1.1b revenue and US$122.1 million earnings by 2029. This implies fairly flat yearly revenue trends and an earnings increase of about US$153.7 million from earnings today of a US$31.6 million loss.

 One alternate view argues that Medical Properties Trust's biggest swing factor is still tenant cash collections, not reported EPS. Before this earnings release, the most bearish analysts were working off flat US$1.1b revenue by 2029 and earnings easing from US$247.6 million to about US$121.1 million. That is a far gloomier arc than the consensus. These projections all pre date the latest profit surprise, so treat them as moving pieces and use them as a prompt to compare several different narratives before committing your own stance.
